Think of movies like books, where you can group things by author or subject matter or period or genre -- so you can focus on Actors or Directors or Subject Matter, for example:

Vietnam:

Platoon -- Directed by Oliver Stone
Full Metal Jacket -- Directed by Stanley Kubrick
Go Tell the Spartans -- Starring Burt Lancaster
Apocalypse Now -- Directed by Francis Ford Coppola

Now from each of these there are quite a few ways you can go on to a new list of movies:

From Platoon you can go on to see more Oliver Stone movies ("JFK" is a personal favorite), or check out actor Willem Dafoe's magnificent portrayal of Christ in "The Last Temptation of Christ".

From Full Metal Jacket you can see more Stanley Kubrick movies ("Barry Lyndon" is visually stunning) or get into some Matthew Modine movies ("Birdy" is great) or even check out Adam Baldwin's first star turn in "My Bodyguard".

From "Go Tell the Spartans" you can watch some Burt Lancaster movies -- Try "Gunfight at the O.K. Corral" with Kirk Douglas and then compare it with the remake "Tombstone" starring Kurt Russell and Val Kilmer. And there's always "Atlantic City" where Susan Sarandon adds to the plot by going topless.

After "Apocalypse Now", you can always watch the Godfather movies directed by Coppola. As a real tangent, consider that "Apocalypse Now" is based on Joseph Conrad's novel "Heart of Darkness". There are two other fine movies based on his books -- "Lord Jim" starring Peter O'Toole, and the less well known "The Secret Agent" starring Bob Hoskins and Gerard Depardieu, with a rarely understated Robin Williams making an uncredited appearance.

You can just go on and on. Have fun.
